Lead · performance

Stock sold through far faster on Saturday, helped by the Men's department

59.2% of inventory had sold through on Saturday 12 September, up from 35.2% the Saturday before1. The Men's department sold 41 more units than a week earlier2; the Briefing called out no other figure.

Why it stands out. Sell-through has climbed for six years, from about 7% in 2020 to over 70% by mid-20263, and it barely varies between departments, brands or distribution centres4. On the days just before, the platform expected 23–38%5. A one-day jump of 24 points is out of character for a measure this steady.

Our read. Treat it as a signal to check, not yet a trend: confirm whether the Men's units were demand or a stock-count change before moving inventory or budget on it.

Sat 5 Sep35.2%Sat 12 Sep59.2%Usual day23–38%
Inventory sell-through, the share of stock that has sold. The usual-day band is the range the platform expected for 7–10 Sep from its own past.

Trends · the longer view

Growth is coming from search and menswear

August revenue rose 13.2% on July, to $396.6K

The investigation credits search traffic and the Men's department6. One reading so far — it shows what changed, not yet what caused it.

Gaps · what we can't see yet

One number has three answers

2025 revenue from completed orders: $608.5K, $610.2K or $2.10M?

Three runs of the same question disagree8. Don't quote a 2025 total until one is confirmed.

Why deliveries run late is still open

There is no carrier-level or warehouse-time data to test it9; the question is parked until 8 Nov.

Cart-to-order conversion isn't measured

The metric is approved but has no formula, so every Briefing leaves it out.

The newest settled day is a month old

theLook settles 29 days late; the last four weeks are still changing in five tables.

For your morning · decide

Three things worth a decision today

Check Saturday's jump before acting on it

Was it Men's demand or a stock count? An investigation can tell.

The last delivery step is slowing

The slowest tenth of deliveries now take 5.0 days, up from 4.010. An investigation is proposed, not run.

Average delivery time is waiting as a metric

Proposed by you from orders; keep it and the Briefing measures it daily.

In brief — what we know

Accessories carry the best margin among the top categories: 59.9% on 7,375 units.
Outerwear & Coats earn the most profit, $741.6K — $158.8K ahead of Jeans.
Men out-earn Women on profit, $231.5K to $181.4K, at near-identical margins (60.0% vs 59.8%).
Skirts are returned most often: 12.5% of items, then Plus and Socks.
Email brings the most users, 52.1K, ahead of Adwords at 39.6K.
Shipped is the largest order state: 37,483 of 124,952 orders.
